title: Enterprise Procurement Architectural Blueprint — Rig Relay
description: Maps industry best practices (SPDX 3.0, CycloneDX 1.7/ECMA-424, SLSA 1.0, OWASP Threat Modeling, OWASP ASVS) to Rig Relay's architecture. Defines implementation waves for enterprise procurement readiness.

research_sources.relevance: SBOM standard for license compliance and software inventory
Full-stack BOM (SBOM, SaaSBOM, VDR, VEX, CDXA attestations). Best fit for Rig's governance/receipt/redaction model
Supply-chain integrity framework. Build provenance, tamper-evident artifacts, verification
Four Question Framework + STRIDE. Continuous threat modeling across software lifecycle

workstreams.title: SBOM Generator + Release Provenance
workstreams.why_cyclonedx_over_spdx: CycloneDX supports SBOM + SaaSBOM + VDR (vulnerability disclosure) + VEX (exploitability exchange) + CDXA (attestations). Rig's governance model (receipts, redaction, content-light evidence) maps directly to CycloneDX's Declarations (compliance-as-code) and Attestations models. SPDX 3.0 is better for license-only compliance; CycloneDX is better for full supply-chain security transparency.

rig_architecture_mapping.existing_capability: Rig already produces schema-validated JSON artifacts with SHA256 hashes, content-light governance, and redaction denylists. The pyproject.toml contains the full dependency tree with versions and licenses.
rig_architecture_mapping.gap: No CycloneDX-formatted SBOM artifact. No SLSA provenance attestation for build artifacts. No signed release pipeline.

files_to_create: rig_relay/enterprise/sbom.py — SBOM generator reading pyproject.toml + uv.lock, producing CycloneDX 1.7 JSON
rig_relay/enterprise/provenance.py — SLSA provenance attestation generator for build artifacts
cyclonedx_fields: components[] — each Python dependency with name, version, purl, licenses, hashes
vulnerabilities[] — placeholder for future Trivy integration
declarations.attestations[] — Rig's existing content-light governance assertions

workstreams.title: Threat Model Artifact (STRIDE over Event Fabric + Bridge + Mutation Path)
workstreams.industry_standard: OWASP Threat Modeling (Four Question Framework + STRIDE) + OWASP ASVS V1 (Architecture)

trust_boundaries.rig_mitigation: Content-light validation rejects forbidden fields before JSONL append. DuckDB is in-memory read-side only — never writes back.
WebSocket is localhost-only. Frontend is dumb renderer — no direct file reads, no unsafe innerHTML. Projection data is content-light.

--execute-remote requires explicit flag, operator checklist acknowledgement, gates-approved. Operation receipts provide non-repudiation. Permission boundary audit proves separation of read/write/alert/PR/file permissions.
Three-clock bridge (heartbeat, status, projection). Backend stale detection triggers degradation, not crash. No event triggers direct mutation.
DuckDB reads read-side only. Queries extract envelope-level fields only. Raw payloads never projected into analytical artifacts.
File-backed coordination with lease IDs, heartbeat TTL, and conflict detection. Stale leases are reclaimed only after confirmed heartbeat miss.

stride_matrix_fields: threat_id, stride_category, trust_boundary, threat_description, affected_components, impact_severity, likelihood, risk_level, existing_mitigations, residual_risk, evidence_refs, recommended_additional_controls

workstreams.title: Container Hardening + Deployment Packaging
workstreams.industry_standard: CIS Docker Benchmark + Kubernetes Pod Security Standards (Restricted) + OWASP ASVS V9 (Communications)

rig_architecture_mapping.existing_capability: Rig has --server-only mode for headless operation. Desktop mode uses pywebview.
rig_architecture_mapping.gap: No Dockerfile, Helm chart, distroless base image, non-root container, read-only filesystem, seccomp profile, or air-gapped install support.

files_to_create: Dockerfile (distroless Python 3.12, non-root user 1000:1000, read-only rootfs, WORKDIR /app)
hardening_checklist: Base image: gcr.io/distroless/python3-debian12 (no shell, no package manager)
Read-only root filesystem (except /tmp and writable volume mounts for .build/, .rig/)
seccomp: runtime/default or custom profile denying mount, ptrace, reboot
AppArmor: deny /proc/sys write, deny capability sys_admin
Readiness probe: HTTP GET /healthz (if exposed) or exec check on bridge status
Liveness probe: TCP socket on WebSocket port

workstreams.title: Merkle Chain over Artifact Receipts (Immutable Audit Trail Proof)
workstreams.industry_standard: SLSA provenance attestations + Certificate Transparency (RFC 6962) — Merkle tree over artifact hashes

rig_architecture_mapping.existing_capability: Every governed artifact carries SHA256 hashes. Operation receipts are append-only JSONL. The replay engine reconstructs pipeline state from artifacts.
rig_architecture_mapping.gap: No merkle tree linking artifact hashes into an immutable chain. No cryptographic proof that the audit trail hasn't been retroactively modified. No root hash that can be published to a transparency log.

files_to_create: rig_relay/enterprise/merkle_chain.py — Merkle tree over artifact hashes
implementation.design: Each governed artifact (inventory, replay, permission audit, causal report, RC report, checklist, runbook) has a SHA256. A merkle tree is built over the sorted list of (artifact_path, sha256) pairs. The root hash is the integrity anchor. A JSON artifact records the tree structure with leaf hashes, sibling hashes, and the root. Periodically (or on release), the root hash is published to a verifiable location.
merkle_fields: chain_id, generated_at, leaf_count, leaves[] (artifact_path, sha256, sequence), root_hash, tree_structure (binary merkle tree with sibling hashes for verification)

workstreams.title: Dependency Vulnerability Scanner Integration
workstreams.industry_standard: CycloneDX VDR (Vulnerability Disclosure Report) + VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange). Tools: Trivy, Grype.

rig_architecture_mapping.existing_capability: pyproject.toml has full dependency tree. uv.lock has pinned versions and hashes.
rig_architecture_mapping.gap: No vulnerability scan in CI. No VDR/VEX artifact. No dependency freshness check.

files_to_create: .github/workflows/dependency-scan.yml — CI job running Trivy on sbom.cdx.json
implementation.ci_integration: On push to main and on PR: generate SBOM → run Trivy → produce VDR artifact → fail CI if CRITICAL vulnerabilities with known fixes exist → produce VEX if vulnerabilities are not exploitable in Rig's context

workstreams.title: RBAC Policy Engine (Evaluable Permission Model)
workstreams.industry_standard: OWASP ASVS V4 (Access Control) + OPA/Rego policy-as-code

rig_architecture_mapping.existing_capability: Rig's permission boundary audit proves separation of read/write/alert/PR/file permissions. Operator checklist has explicit operator acknowledgements.
rig_architecture_mapping.gap: No evaluable RBAC policy. Permissions are documented in JSON artifacts but not enforced by a policy engine. No OIDC/SAML group mapping.

implementation.rbac_design: Model: subject (user/OIDC group) → role (operator, reviewer, auditor, admin) → permission (read_event_fabric, publish_event, execute_live_mutation, view_spiderweb, modify_alert_rules, approve_gates). Each permission maps to a Rig operation. Policy evaluation: given (subject, role, operation, resource), return {allowed: true/false, reason: string, required_role: string}. Integrates with operator checklist — the 'gates-approved' flag is only true when the subject's role permits the operation.
rbac_fields: policy_id, version, roles[] (role_name, description, permissions[]), subjects[] (subject_id, provider, roles[]), operations[] (operation_id, description, required_permissions[], gate_ids[])

implementation_waves.title: P0 Foundation — SBOM + Threat Model
acceptance_criteria: CycloneDX 1.7 SBOM artifact validates against ECMA-424 schema
SBOM includes all pyproject.toml dependencies with purl, version, license, hash
SLSA Build Level 2 provenance attestation for the Rig Relay wheel
STRIDE threat model covers 6 trust boundaries with mitigations mapped to existing Rig subsystems
Threat model artifact validates against schema

implementation_waves.title: P1 Security — Container Hardening + Merkle Chain
acceptance_criteria: Distroless Dockerfile builds and runs rig-relay --server-only
Container passes Kubernetes Restricted Pod Security Standard
Helm chart deploys to minikube/kind without errors
Merkle chain covers all Phase 2 governance artifacts
Merkle verification CLI detects a tampered artifact hash
Root hash is deterministic for unchanged artifacts

implementation_waves.title: P2 Compliance — Dependency Scan + RBAC
implementation_waves.dependencies: Wave 1 (SBOM needed for Trivy), Wave 2 (container for CI integration)
acceptance_criteria: CI workflow runs Trivy on SBOM, produces VDR artifact
CI fails on CRITICAL vulnerabilities with known fixes
RBAC policy evaluator denies execute_live_mutation for reviewer role
Policy evaluation is deterministic and content-light
OIDC group mapping is configurable via environment

enterprise_procurement_checklist_mapping.vendor_security_questionnaire: P0-SBOM (CycloneDX with component inventory) + P0-THREAT (STRIDE threat model) + P2-SCAN (VDR showing known vulnerabilities)
enterprise_procurement_checklist_mapping.penetration_test_scope: P0-THREAT (trust boundaries define pen test targets: WebSocket channel, mutation executor, DuckDB read path, event fabric JSONL)
enterprise_procurement_checklist_mapping.deployment_security_review: P1-CONTAINER (hardened Dockerfile, Helm chart, seccomp/AppArmor, non-root, read-only FS)
enterprise_procurement_checklist_mapping.compliance_audit: P1-MERKLE (immutable audit trail proof) + P2-RBAC (evaluable access control)
enterprise_procurement_checklist_mapping.third_party_risk_assessment: P0-SBOM (dependency inventory with licenses) + P2-SCAN (vulnerability scan on every dependency)
enterprise_procurement_checklist_mapping.access_control_review: P2-RBAC (role-based policy engine, OIDC/SAML group mapping)

dependencies_to_consider.purpose: Generate CycloneDX 1.7 SBOM programmatically. Lightweight, official OWASP library.
dependencies_to_consider.alternative: Generate JSON directly from pyproject.toml + uv.lock without dependency

dependencies_to_consider.purpose: Vulnerability scanner. Runs as CI step, not Python dependency.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: CycloneDX 1.7 is ECMA-424 — a very new standard. Some procurement teams may still expect SPDX.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Support both. Generate SPDX 3.0 (JSON) for license compliance and CycloneDX 1.7 for security transparency. The SBOM.py module can produce both formats.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Merkle chain root hash publication requires a transparency log or verifiable location. Without it, the chain is locally verifiable but not publicly auditable.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Publish root hash in the release GitHub Release notes (immutable once published). For enterprise, integrate with Sigstore/rekor transparency log.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Container hardening requires ongoing maintenance — distroless images update, CVEs are patched, base image tags rot.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: CI workflow rebuilds container on every push to main. Dependabot/renovate watches base image tags. SBOM regeneration on every build captures updated component inventory.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: RBAC policy engine without OPA/Rego may not satisfy enterprise customers who expect industry-standard policy-as-code.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Phase 1 uses a native Python evaluator (lightweight, no new dependency). Phase 2 can add OPA sidecar with Rego policies. The RBAC model is designed to be translatable to Rego.

recommended_execution_sequence: Execute Wave 1 (P0) immediately — produces procurement-readable SBOM and threat model. Wave 2 (P1) after first real live mutation succeeds. Wave 3 (P2) as part of first enterprise pilot deployment.
